venture.headline: Isomorphic Labs raises $5B as it looks to take drug candidates to clinical trials
venture.summary: Isomorphic Labs, the AI drug-discovery platform that was spun out of Google’s DeepMind in 2021, has raised $5 Billion in a Series C funding round.

venture.summary: Science Corp raised a $400 million Series D to scale up its anti-blindness business.

venture.headline: Cybersecurity AI startup Corma reaches $1B valuation in about 3 months
venture.summary: Three months since introducing its product, AI cybersecurity startup Corba has raised a $125 million Series A at a $1 billion valuation led by NEA.

research.headline: ViRA: Toward Ultra-High-Resolution Visual Agents via Cross-Input Relative Policy Optimization
research.summary: Visual agents answer questions about ultra-high-resolution photos by zooming into the relevant regions. However, existing agents often answer from common sense instead of reading the evidence. Reinforcement learning (RL) on the final answer cannot correct this, because a guess earns the same reward as reading.

research.headline: Beyond Job Titles: Interpreting Early-Career Job Advertisements with Sparse Autoencoders and Semantic Clustering
research.summary: Job titles and job descriptions alone provide limited insight into how technical roles differ in a changing job market. To assess how such roles differ in their work and industry applications, we design and compare two methods based on deep learning and transformer representations using 36,081 early-career job postings collected from LinkedIn in the United States between December 2025 and October 2026. We first apply PERC, short for Preprocessing (P), Embedding (E), Dimensionality Reduction (R) and Clustering (C).

research.headline: Hyperlyve: Parallelized Enumeration and Exact Lyapunov Stability Certification for Deep ReLU Networks
research.summary: We introduce Hyperlyve (Hyperplane Partitioned Lyapunov Verification and Enumeration), a framework for proving the asymptotic stability of nonlinear dynamical systems, including those with neural network controllers. Hyperlyve learns and formally certifies continuous piecewise-affine (CPA) neural Lyapunov functions within a counterexample-guided inductive synthesis (CEGIS) loop. Hyperlyve's key innovation is a parallel algorithm that enumerates the hyperplane arrangement formed by the ReLU activations of deep networks and certifies that Lyapunov conditions hold within each polyhedral region.

research.headline: Quantifying the added value of human forecaster discussions for tropical cyclone intensity prediction
research.summary: The National Hurricane Center routinely releases Tropical Cyclone Discussions that offer insights into its tropical cyclone forecasts. This study examines the added value of these discussions for intensity forecasting beyond a set of numerical predictors. For 637 Atlantic and eastern North Pacific tropical cyclones from the 2002-2023 hurricane seasons, we analyze the discussion text and its combination with 13 hurricane environmental predictors from SHIPS and ERA5 10-meter wind fields, for forecasting intensity changes at lead times of 24 to 120 hours using three modeling methods.

titans.summary: Jensen Huang's stunning resignation from Nvidia after more than 33 years has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. regulatory.headline: FTC Sues to Block Covetrus Acquisition of MWI Veterinary Supply
regulatory.summary: The Federal Trade Commission filed a lawsuit to block Covetrus Inc. from acquiring its closest competitor, MWI Veterinary Supply Inc., in a $3.5 billion deal. The FTC alleges the merger of the two largest veterinary product distributors will increase costs and raise prices for clinics and pet owners.

regulatory.headline: FTC and 17 States Secure $63 Million Settlement with Family Dollar Stores in Price Transparency Win for Consumers
regulatory.summary: Family Dollar has generated millions of dollars by charging more at the register than the prices it advertises, the FTC and states allege Family Dollar will pay $63 million to settle Federal Trade Commission and state allegations that the company routinely charged customers more at the register than the prices displayed on shelves, price tags and advertisements, costing consumers millions of dollars.

regulatory.headline: Five States Join FTC Lawsuit Alleging Hims and Hers Engaged in Deceptive and Unlawful Privacy Practices
regulatory.summary: The Federal Trade Commission filed an amended complaint adding five states as co-plaintiffs in its lawsuit alleging that telehealth provider Hims and Hers shared consumers’ sensitive health information with third-party advertising platforms, despite claiming its services maintain consumers’ privacy, and it deceived users about its billing and cancellation practices.

frontier.headline: Resolving and Suppressing Temporally Correlated Noise in Quantum Error Correction
frontier.summary: Scaling fault-tolerant quantum error correction (QEC) requires suppressing errors in both space and time, yet standard logical memory experiments primarily probe spatial faults. Here, we use a 105-qubit Willow superconducting quantum processor to realize and scale the surface code stability experiment, which is alternatively sensitive to temporal error chains. Scaling from patch sizes of $3 \times 3$ to $7 \times 7$, we realize a timelike block suppression factor of $μ_T = 1.47 \pm 0.25$, demonstrating the ability to maintain temporal error suppression as the number of qubits increases.

frontier.headline: A mysterious twist in the universe’s oldest light could reveal new physics
frontier.summary: Scientists have spotted hints of a mysterious rotation in the universe’s oldest light that could reveal new physics and shed light on dark matter and dark energy. A new technique developed at UC San Diego could help rule out misleading telescope errors, bringing researchers closer to determining whether the strange signal is real.

frontier.headline: Exponential Quantum Memory Advantage for Late-Graph Smoothness and Spectral Estimation
frontier.summary: Graph signal processing tests how smoothly the decisions of next-generation massive sensor networks with $N$ nodes vary over their neighbour graph. Memory becomes the bottleneck when the neighbour graph arrives only after data erasure, a late-graph setting motivated by dispersed sensor networks and telemetry. We analyse three collection scenarios, reliable rounds, continuous broadcast and ordered capture, and test the Dirichlet energy $\mathcal E_G=\mathbf z^{\mathsf T}\mathbf L\mathbf z/N$ of the fused decision map $\mathbf z\in\{\pm1\}^N$, with late-graph Laplacian $\mathbf L$, against two thresholds.

frontier.headline: Cannabis addiction linked to 57% higher odds of suicidal thoughts
frontier.summary: A massive study involving more than 415,000 Americans has uncovered a concerning connection between cannabis use disorder and suicidal thoughts. Researchers found that adults with the disorder had 57% higher odds of experiencing suicidal thoughts, with women and younger adults facing particularly elevated risks.

frontier.headline: Optimal Quantum Sensing Algorithms for Discrete-Frequency Spectroscopy
frontier.summary: Spectroscopy is a versatile tool that drives scientific discovery and underpins modern technologies. Quantum sensing offers promising opportunities to advance spectroscopy through enhanced sensitivity and spectral and spatial resolution. However, existing approaches largely focus on improving general measurement capabilities, often overlooking the structure of specific sensing tasks and leaving potential performance gains untapped.

industry.headline: This Startup Is Betting on AI Microdramas to Get More Black Stories in Hollywood
industry.summary: Mansa says its AI microdramas can serve as proofs of concept for what Black audiences want. Critics say the studio is selling out.

voices.headline: The Only Thing Nathan Fielder Won’t Show
voices.summary: Y ou Can See Everything has given America a new villain: Billy Evans. The blockbuster documentary, created by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, is about Elizabeth Holmes, the former CEO of the blood-test company Theranos, and the days before she reports to federal prison after being convicted of fraud. But Evans, her partner and the father of her two children, manages to come out of the film looking worse than she does—not because he committed any crime, but because he wanted to get paid for participating in the documentary.

voices.headline: Don’t Be So Surprised That Mississippi Turned Blue
voices.summary: ET on November 16, 2026 Scott Colom, the first Black U.S. senator ever elected by Mississippians, traces his lineage in the state back seven generations, to when the nation was forging its foundation on the backs of stolen Black people. He waged a campaign set on showing that “Mississippi matters,” which many registered more as a question than a declaration, doubting whether a Black man and a Democrat could win the seat.
